faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: I see the message Service Request 00010004 - 000101D. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Service Request errors in the range 00010004 - 000101D are related to a carriage movement problem. In some instances like paper jams, the carriage locking tab may be partially pushed in, causing the carriage locking mechanism to put a drag on the carriage or lock the carriage completely. This will cause any of the carriage errors. Make sure the carriage locking tab is pulled all the way out. Then turn the printer's power off and release the carriage by pushing down on the cutter blade. Slide the carriage to the left and look for any paper that also may be restricting the carriage from moving freely.
00010004
CR Motor encoder check error
00010005
CR Motor out of step
00010006
CR Motor over current
00010007
CR Motor in-position time-out
0001000A
CR axis detection error
0001000F
CR Motor PWM output faulty
0001001D
CR servo parameter error
The T-Fence can also be dirty or out of the carriage encoder. Check to make sure it is clean and in the center of the encoder. Contact Epson for additional assistance.
The current firmware corrects erroneous Service Request 00010007, which occurs after the power is first turned on. You can download this firmware upgrade from www.prographics.epson.com.

faqs.question: What does the message Service Req. 00010030 mean?
faqs.answer: This is a multi-sensor failure error. The multi-sensor is an optical sensor that detects the amount of light to determine if print media is loaded correctly in the printer.  An excessive amount of light may cause this error to appear. Make sure the printer is not in direct sunlight.

faqs.question: What does the message Service Req. OD100102 mean?

Turn off the printer and make sure the paper hopper is locked in the down position. The error message should be cleared when you turn the printer on again.

faqs.question: Why do I see a difference in ink level reporting?
faqs.answer:
Ink levels are a calculated value based on the average amount of ink used for printing at different dot sizes, performing cleaning cycles, printer initialization, borderless printing, nozzle checks and other dot fire sequences. The ink levels are reported as follows:
The control panel ink gauge represents ink levels in 20% steps. The first level will be displayed for an ink level of anywhere from 100% to 80%, the next level 80% to 60%, and so on.
When a print job is sent, the Status Monitor reads and displays the current ink levels at that point in time.
Depending on when and which method you use to view ink levels, they can easily appear to be giving different ink level information at that point in time. The Status Monitor provides the most accurate ink level information.

faqs.question: If I don't use roll paper do I need to have the roll paper holder attached?
faqs.answer: No. The printer will work without the roll paper holder installed. The holder is designed to be removed easily.

faqs.question: What is the minimum paper size I can use with my product?
faqs.answer: 8 x 10 inches.

faqs.question: My product recently started having trouble loading paper. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
You may need to clean the pickup rollers. Do the following:
Turn on the printer and remove any loaded paper.
Remove the paper tray so you can see the pickup rollers and roller covers.
Note
: The left side pickup roller may be in a different location than shown above, since it moves with the left side paper guide.
Clean the light grey areas beneath the roller covers.
We recommend using cotton swabs dampened with water to clean dust from the rollers. Be sure to allow ample time for the rollers to dry before loading paper.
To clean each roller's surface completely, they must be rotated. Press the
down arrow button on the printer's control panel to rotate the rollers; watch for a moment to see how the gears inside the printer are engaged when the rollers are moving. Be careful not to get anything stuck in between the rollers.
Rotate the rollers a little at a time, cleaning the exposed roller surface between rotations.

faqs.question: Why is my product having a problem detecting tracing paper?
faqs.answer: Tracing paper support is improved in the latest firmware. You can download this firmware upgrade from www.prographics.epson.com. The firmware also adds a 10mm top margin and the loading speed is slowed down when tracing paper is used.

faqs.question: I'm getting a crease in my roll media. What should I do?
faqs.answer: A crease in roll media is the result of the paper feed roller holding the media for a long time. Remove the roll media from the paper path when you have finished using it to prevent the media from being creased.

faqs.question: How can I prevent paper from jamming or misfeeding from the paper tray?
faqs.answer:
Fan the paper and tap it on a flat surface to even the edges.
If you need to add paper to the paper tray, first remove all paper from the tray and then add paper to the removed stack.
If your paper is curled, flatten it before you load it. If it curls excessively and jams frequently, stop using it.
Load the sheets with the printable side face down and the right edge of the paper resting against the right side of the paper tray. Make sure the sheets lie flat on the bottom of the tray.
Do not over fill the paper tray.
When you load sheets of paper, place the edge of the paper against the right inner corner of the paper tray. Otherwise, printing may become misaligned.
Adjust the paper guide and edge guide according to the paper size. They must be snug against the paper.
Put the paper guide roller down and replace the paper tray cover.

faqs.question: When I print on roll paper, my image prints too far to the left. What should I do?

faqs.question: How can I prevent smeared ink and droplets on my printouts?
faqs.answer:
The print head can gather dust over time, which then gathers ink. This accumulated ink can get deposited on the substrate during printing. Cleaning the wiper blade and pump cap assembly can solve this problem. Do the following:
Turn off the printer.
Open the top cover and press the cutter solenoid down to release the print head.
Note
: This photo shows the Pro 4800 cutter solenoid assembly; the assembly in the Pro 4000 is black.
Move the print head to the left.
Locate the wiper blade and clean it with a moist cotton swab.
Note
: Most of the wiper blade is located behind the clear plastic shield, which may be difficult to clean. If you use a long cotton swab you'll be able to reach further back and clean the blade more thoroughly. The blade is split down the middle so be sure to clean both sides of the blade and inside the split.
Inspect the foam pad area of the pump cap assembly for any large pieces of debris and gently remove them with a moist cotton swab. Then use the swab to gently wipe the topside frame of the plastic housing that holds the multi-colored foam pad.
Caution
: Do not try to remove the foam pad.
The flushing box next to the multi-colored cap assembly does not typically come in contact with the print head, but you should gently clean any debris that may have accumulated there.
Close the top cover and turn on the printer.
Print a
nozzle check
and inspect the printed pattern.
If the nozzle check pattern looks good, you are ready to print; you don't need to continue with the following steps.
If the nozzle check pattern is not satisfactory, continue with the next step.
If the nozzle check pattern is not satisfactory, run a cleaning cycle and print another nozzle check. In the printer utility, be sure to select
Print
(not
Auto
) for the nozzle check.
If the nozzle check pattern is still not complete, repeat step 9 until you see a good nozzle check pattern or you have run three cleaning cycles.
If the nozzle check pattern looks good, you are ready to print.
If the nozzle check pattern still is not good after running three cleaning cycles, contact Epson Technical Support for further assistance.

faqs.question: When I try to print color separations using ColorBurst for Windows, the RIP produces a composite print where the separations are re-combined. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer:
The Windows version of ColorBurst produces the separations as a composite print that shows traps and overprint. This feature cannot be disabled.
The Macintosh version of ColorBurst can be used with the Stylus Pro 4000 to produce color separations with individual layers of color per page.

faqs.answer: No.

faqs.question: When I created a ColorBurst hot folder on my Mac desktop, all of my desktop icons were transferred into the print queue. What should I do?
faqs.answer: To create a hot folder on your desktop, create a new folder, then assign this folder as the hot folder. If you assign the desktop as the hot folder, every desktop icon will be sent to the print queue.

faqs.question: After I print a file by dragging it to the ColorBurst hot folder, my file is no longer in the hot folder. What happened?
faqs.answer: This is normal. Once the file prints from the hot folder, you cannot go back to the hot folder to reprint the job. To print the file again, drag it into the hot folder again.

faqs.question: I don't see a Media Type setting for Epson Premium Luster Photo Paper (260) in the Epson driver. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Download the latest printer driver, the latest firmware, and the ICC profiles from the Downloads tab for your product.

faqs.question: Why doesn't the Supplies button function properly?
faqs.answer:
The
Supplies
button is an Apple function and is not currently supported by Epson.

faqs.question: When I send a print job to the ColorBurst RIP, I see the queued job, but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
When printing from Windows, verify that the spooler is started.  The
Start Spooler
option is on the menu bar. The spooler has to be started each time ColorBurst is launched.
When printing from a Macintosh, verify that the RIP is set to
RIP ON
and make sure
Receive On Hold
is not selected.

faqs.question: How can I tell if I have the Epson version or the full version of ColorBurst?
faqs.answer:
There are two ways to tell if you have the Epson version:
When you launch ColorBurst, look at the splash screen. The Epson version has a message
Provided by Epson America Inc.
at the top right.
The Epson version has an
Epson Technical Support
option under the
HELP
menu.

faqs.question: What is the Super (X) setting in the Epson driver?
faqs.answer: This is a Super Microweave setting that enables the print head to perform 8 microweave passes instead of the standard 4 passes. The through-put is slowed with this setting. However, it produces the highest quality prints when you use it along with the highest print resolutions of 1440 or 2880 with the high speed setting turned off.

faqs.question: The Advanced B/W setting is grayed out in my product software. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure you install the correct black ink cartridge for the media type selected. When the photo black cartridge is installed, the
Advanced B/W
setting is available only for glossy media types. It is not available for any of the matte media types. When the matte black cartridge is installed, the
Advanced B/W
setting is available only for matte media types.
If you're using the correct black ink cartridge for your media type but the
Advanced B/W
setting is still grayed out, then Do the following:
Open the
Hard Drive
.
Select >
Applications
>
Utilities
>
Printer Setup Utility
.
Select your printer and click
Utility
.
Make sure you see the ink levels in the
Status Monitor
window, then click
Update
.
Restart the computer.

faqs.question: How can I get a replacement ColorBurst CD if mine is lost or damaged?
faqs.answer: Epson will replace the lost or damaged CD free of charge. Proof of purchase is required to verify product code. You must have purchased the Stylus Pro 4000 Pro Bundle (C511001PRO) to qualify for a free replacement.

faqs.question: What Media Type do I select in the Epson driver for Ultra Smooth Fine Art paper?
faqs.answer:
Choose the
Water Color - Radiant White
for the Media Type.

faqs.question: How can I share my product with other users?
faqs.answer:
We recommend sharing your printer via an Ethernet connection with the optional Epson High Speed Ethernet Print Server card (part number C12C823912 or C12C824052). This method provides many benefits, including better performance, over selecting
Printer Sharing
for a locally attached Stylus Pro 4000 printer.

faqs.question: Can I turn off color management for ColorBurst?
faqs.answer: Color management cannot be turned off or disabled.  It is activated by default.

faqs.question: How do I stop the printer from printing a nozzle check pattern before every print job?
faqs.answer:
Do the following on the product's control panel:
Press
Menu
twice, then select
Auto Nozzle Check
.
Press
Menu
, then select
Off

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Illustrator?
faqs.answer:
For the best output, a RIP should be used. Adobe Illustrator is a postscript application that requires a RIP to translate the postscript language. The printer comes with a non-postscript driver that has difficulty translating the postscript language.
Epson has partnered with the following manufacturers for some printers:
ColorBurst
efi
Onyx
Wasatch

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Photoshop?
faqs.answer: No, Adobe Photoshop is not a postscript application and does not require a RIP.

faqs.question: How do I save my Epson printer driver presets so I can restore them if I reinstall the Epson printer driver in Windows?
faqs.answer:
Note:
You may lose some custom settings when you uninstall the printer driver.
Before you reinstall the printer driver, do the following:
Open

or
Windows Explorer
.

or

drive >

>
Epson
> [your printer name].
Move the UCI extension files to a different folder on your desktop.
Note:
After you reinstall the Epson printer driver, move the UCI extension files back to your printer's folder as described in step 2.

faqs.question: How do I install the ICC profiles in Windows XP or Windows 7?
faqs.answer:

color
folder, then close all open windows.

faqs.question: Does Epson make drivers for Linux?
faqs.answer:
Linux drivers are available for some products. Visit the links below to see the drivers available for your product, as well as information about using an Epson product with Linux.

Epson does not provide support for Linux drivers.
Linux drivers for Epson products
Linux FAQs for Epson products

faqs.question: When should I use the MK4 printer profile suffix?
faqs.answer: The MK4 printer profile suffix refers to the dual CMYK configuration for the Stylus Pro 4000. The dual CMYK Stylus Pro 4000 in not sold in the North American market.

faqs.question: I'm trying to perform a ColorBurst client install on my PC. Why can't I see the server computer when I browse the network?
faqs.answer:
To perform a client install successfully, you need to share the printer on the server computer. Otherwise, you will not be able to add the client. To share the printer on the server, Do the following:
Click
Start
>
Settings
>
Printers and Faxes
. (Windows XP)
Right-click the ColorBurst RIP icon.
Click
Sharing
, then select
Share this printer
.
Click
OK
.

faqs.question: Why is my product making a loud humming sound all the time?
faqs.answer: The printer has suction fans to hold the paper flat in the paper path and an exhaust fan for cooling at the rear of the unit. The humming sound can be heard when the fans turn on. The current firmware turns the fans off when the printer is in idle mode. With previous versions of the firmware, the fans stayed on all the time. You can download the latest firmware from Downloads tab.

faqs.question: Which interfaces can I use to connect my product when using ColorBurst?
faqs.answer: You can use a USB, IEEE 1394 (FireWire), or Ethernet connection when operating in a Windows environment. When operating in a Mac environment, you can use either a USB or Ethernet connection.

faqs.question: How do I get service for my product I purchased in another country?
faqs.answer: Due to differences in products sold in other countries, printers need to be serviced in the country of origin.

faqs.question: I hear a grinding noise when I turn on my product. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the green carriage locking tab is pulled out away from the carriage and there is nothing obstructing the carriage.

faqs.question: How do I read the Job History Log?
faqs.answer:
The job history log has ten entries numbered 0 - 9 for the last 10 print jobs.
The current job is stored in location 0, the oldest job is in location 9.
If the log is full, the current job is recorded in location 0, and the older jobs are pushed down one location. The oldest job history information that was in location 9 is lost.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: Where do I find my product's serial number?
faqs.answer:
See our
Finding Your Epson Product Serial Number
page for details.
